PRIMARY CARE NOTE   Date: 2026-04-10
57M, ambulatory visit for an annual check-up.

S:
Patient presents for a routine check-up. He reports occasional wheezing with exertion and dust exposure, well managed with his reliever. Over the past two months he has had intermittent joint aches in the hands and wrists with some morning stiffness and a few episodes of a sun-sensitive facial rash, prompting further workup today. Diet is high in sugary drinks, which was discussed. He works as a carpenter. Lives with his spouse. Never smoker, rare alcohol.

O:
BP 124/78, HR 72, RR 14, Temp 98.2 F, SpO2 98% on room air. Weight 188 lb, BMI 28.
General: well appearing, in no acute distress.
HEENT: nasal mucosa normal, mild redness over sun-exposed skin of the face.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally at rest.
Musculoskeletal: mild tenderness at the wrists, full range of motion, no effusion.
Skin: faint sunburn-like redness over the cheeks.
Labs (prior week): A1c 6.1%, CBC within normal limits, ANA negative, basic metabolic panel normal.

A/P:
1. Asthma, uncomplicated, using inhaler as needed. Continue short-acting reliever before exertion; inhaler technique reviewed and adequate. Provided a written action plan and advised a dust mask at work.
2. Rule out lupus; ANA negative. Facial redness fits sun exposure and the joint aches fit repetitive hand use; no further autoimmune testing or rheumatology referral needed. Advised sun protection.
3. Prediabetes, counseled on diet and exercise. Reviewed reducing sugary drinks and adding regular walks. Recheck A1c in 6 months.
4. Health maintenance: colorectal screening discussed and up to date; influenza vaccine offered in the fall.

Return in 3 months, sooner if the rash spreads or new joint swelling develops.
